8864.full: Carnegie Public Library · Long Eaton Library

stories.text: The town's new wealth shows in its Art Nouveau buildings: York Chambers of 1901 and the Midland Counties District Bank of 1903, at 38 and 40 Market Place, and the Carnegie Library on Tamworth Road of 1906, by the same architects, Gorman and Ross. York Chambers and the library are listed Grade II.

8864.sum: Carnegie Public Library, on Tamworth Road. Today it houses Long Eaton Library. The building was built in 1906, according to Wikidata. It is Grade II listed.

stories.text: Harrington Mill, one of the largest lace mills, was built in 1885. It took one and a quarter million bricks to build, and is 167 metres long.

aka: Church of St Laurence and St James

stories.text: Domesday Book calls the village Aitone. Its church of St Laurence stands east of the Market Place: local tradition dates parts of it to the 11th century and King Cnut, but its oldest parts may be from after the Conquest, in the 12th century. It was a daughter church of Sawley until the 19th century. It is listed Grade II*.

14093.sum: St. Laurence's Church, Long Eaton, is a Grade II* listed parish church in Long Eaton, England. 11th century
